subject: Advance commitment amendment: ramp schedule and termination redlines
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@aurorahealthtech.com>, Aurora HealthTech Procurement <procurement@aurorahealthtech.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Advance commitment proposal — 3yr annual prepay + ramp schedule

Hi Samuel / team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — really excited by the use case you outlined for inference at scale. Per our conversation, attached is a customer-friendly amendment that converts your current subscription into a three-year commitment with annual prepay, a structured ramp (year 1 = 40% of committed units, year 2 = 70%, year 3 = 100%), and the pricing tiers / term discounts we discussed.

Highlights:
- Term: 36 months with annual prepay invoices
- Effective discount: 18% on list in year 1 (ramped), 22% year 2, 28% year 3 based on commitment bands
- Early termination: draft proposes a pro-rated refund on unused prepay less an administrative recovery (placeholder % to be confirmed)
- Co-terming: optional true-up on renewal to align end-dates if you want everything to end on the same cycle

I attached a draft amendment (RDW_AdvanceCommitment_Amendment_v3.pdf) and an example amortization schedule (amortization_schedule_v2.xlsx) so your finance team can see how the credits/true-ups look across quarters.

Could you confirm: 1) whether your procurement needs a specific co-term date (you mentioned 3/31/2028 as a possible anchor), and 2) whether Aurora would prefer a fixed termination fee or a pro-rata refund approach? If you prefer, we can have legal swap a flat fee for a pro-rata formula.

Next step: if internal OK, we can iterate on legal redlines and I’ll loop Olga for any commercial exceptions.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0199
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@aurorahealthtech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora HealthTech Procurement <procurement@aurorahealthtech.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Advance commitment proposal — 3yr annual prepay + ramp schedule

Rishi —

Thanks for the draft. A few immediate questions from procurement/finance:

1) Early termination: we need clarity on the refund calculation. Our controller will not accept open-ended administrative charges; we typically ask for a formula that ties to the time remaining on term (pro rata) with a hard cap (e.g., no more than 20% deducted).
2) Co-terming: we do want to align the commitments where possible. Our current master ends on 2028-03-31; if we prepay annually starting 2026-07-01, the co-term mechanics matter (how do we handle partial-year credits when syncing cycles?).
3) Audit / escrow: for multi-year prepay some of our stakeholders prefer an escrow or bank guarantee for the portion beyond 12 months. Any flexibility there?

Also please have your legal explain how refunds are handled if we exercise termination for convenience vs material breach.

Can you include your proposed amortization and the actual refund formula in the next version? We’ll share this internally with Elena (cc) who handles contracts.

—Samuel
Director, Procurement — Aurora HealthTech
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@aurorahealthtech.com>, Aurora HealthTech Procurement <procurement@aurorahealthtech.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Advance commitment proposal — 3yr annual prepay + ramp schedule

Samuel / Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and proposed edits:

1) Refund calculation (draft): remaining prepay value * (months remaining / total months in prepay year) - administrative recovery. Proposed administrative recovery = 15% of remaining prepay value (we can adjust). We’ll swap "administrative recovery" for explicit language and a hard cap as you requested.
2) Co-terming: propose a simple true-up credit at the next annual invoice to align your cycles (example in amortization spreadsheet). If you want all contracts to end 2028-03-31, we can add a pro rata reconciliation triggered on that date.
3) Escrow: we don’t typically use escrow for hosted customers. Options: (A) a letter of credit for amounts > 12 months, (B) restricted refund reserve on our side with reporting, or (C) shortened commit window for a tranche of the spend. Happy to provide standard language for a letter of credit if that’s the path.

I’ve attached the amendment and amortization schedule again with inline comments. Please have Elena & legal share redlines; I’ve looped Olga for any commercial exceptions (she can sign off on discount / recovery adjustments).

Thanks — I’ll stand by for your legal redlines.

Best,
Rishi
From: Elena Park <elena.park@aurorahealthtech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@aurorahealthtech.com>
Cc: Aurora HealthTech Procurement <procurement@aurorahealthtech.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Advance commitment proposal — redlines attached

Rishi —

Attached are initial redlines (redline_contract_aurora.docx). High-level items from legal/procurement: 

- Early termination: we prefer a pro rata refund for unused services with a capped admin charge. Request cap at 12% (not to exceed).
- Termination for convenience vs breach: in breach scenarios, allow Redwood to offset only proven damages; in convenience cases, we expect the pro rata formula (no additional penalties beyond cap).
- Co-terming: propose explicit language that any annual prepay year that ends early because of co-terming will receive a pro rata credit applied to the subsequent invoice; if the next invoice is not issued within 90 days, apply cash refund.
- Escrow/guarantee: Aurora would accept a bank letter of credit for amounts > 12 months. Please confirm Redwood has an LC template.

We also flagged the admin recovery term (15%) and would like it reduced to 12%.

Please have your legal review and propose redline language.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Senior Counsel, Aurora HealthTech
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Advance commitment proposal — suggested legal compromise

Olga / Rishi —

I reviewed Aurora's redlines and drafted compromise language to move the deal forward. Key points:

1) Early termination refund: refund equals (prepaid amount for unused months) * (remaining months / months in prepay year) less administrative recovery of 15% — but Redwood can offer a one-time commercial concession to reduce the administrative recovery to 12% for this customer if commercial approves.

2) Cap mechanics: not necessary if we set an explicit administrative recovery percentage and tighten definitions for "unused months". A hard cap introduces accounting complexity and unpredictable recognition. Proposal: accept Aurora's ask in effect (12% admin recovery) as a commercial concession.

3) Co-terming: propose the true-up credit approach. Implementation detail: create a quarterly reconciliation schedule; if reconciliation yields a credit and customer requests cash within 90 days, process refund.

4) Escrow/LC: we can provide an LC template but prefer a restricted refund reserve in our ledger. If Aurora insists on LC for >12 months we will accept, but require standard LC fees to be borne by Aurora.

Commercial ask: Olga — can you approve the 12% administrative recovery concession and authority to accept LC fees charged to customer? If yes I’ll incorporate final redline language and sign off.

Attached is the redline with legal comments (redline_contract_aurora.docx).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@aurorahealthtech.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@aurorahealthtech.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Advance commitment proposal — final commercial concession and next steps

Samuel / Elena —

Thanks for the thorough notes and for being flexible on mechanics. We want to get this done in a way that protects both sides and keeps your team productive. Commercial decisions: 

- Redwood will accept your co-terming mechanics and the quarterly true-up process described.
- We will reduce the administrative recovery to 12% (one-time concession) for Aurora on this amendment.
- We can accept a bank letter of credit for amounts beyond 12 months; Aurora will cover LC issuance/maintenance fees. If you prefer, we can also publish a restricted refund reserve schedule from our side — let us know which you prefer.

Next steps:
1) Rishi will send the DocuSign-ready amendment (finalized redlines incorporated) by end of day tomorrow.
2) Please provide your PO and billing contact; the invoice for year 1 will be issued upon counter-signature.
3) We will update HubSpot: Deal DL-2026-0471 -> Contract Signed (pending payment). Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/471-aurora

I’ll also CC finance (Vivek) for any amortization questions. Looking forward to partnering.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Americas — Redwood Inference
Phone: (510) 555-0123
